messages:
Jordan: Hey team — escalating: customer acct-9876 seeing intermittent decrypt failures hitting our API when they run bulk ingest (concurrency ~150-300). Started 03/12 09:10UTC. Error from our side shows HSM returns CKR_DEVICE_ERROR intermittently. Need triage + compliance check (audit logs).
Priya: thanks — can you paste the minimal repro and a short log snippet? also which HSM (CloudHSM vs on-prem) and cluster id?
Jordan: CloudHSM cluster: arn:aws:cloudhsm:us-east-1:123456:cluster/cls-0a1b2c3d. Repro: run 200 parallel decrypts against /v1/crypto/decrypt. Curl (simplified):
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/crypto/decrypt -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"kid":"key-45","ct":"..."}' &
done
wait
```
Response snapshot when failing: HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":"hsm_decrypt_error","details":"CKR_DEVICE_ERROR (0x00000006)"}
Jordan: log snippet from host handling request (redwood-crypto-02):
```
2026-03-12T09:12:13.243Z ERROR hsm_client: decrypt failed, rv=0x6
2026-03-12T09:12:13.244Z WARN  hsm_session_pool: session checkout failed after retries
2026-03-12T09:12:13.245Z INFO  metrics: concurrent_sessions=162, pool_size=160
```
Ethan: looks like pool exhaustion + device error. CloudHSM can surface CKR_DEVICE_ERROR during maintenance/soft restart / failover. Do we have CloudHSM cluster events around 09:12?
Jordan: pulling AWS CloudTrail/CloudHSM events now — found cluster event: 2026-03-12T09:11:58Z "HA failover: node(2) -> node(1)" and corresponding instance reboot a couple seconds later. OpsBot also posted an alert:
OpsBot: [ALERT] cloudhsm-cls-0a1b2c3d failover detected at 2026-03-12T09:11:58Z (id=evt-789)
Priya: so likely client saw transient device errors while HSM restarted and our session pool didn't gracefully handle in-flight ops. Two asks: 1) collect HSM audit logs for the window (09:10-09:15 UTC) for compliance review; 2) safe mitigation to avoid data exposure / key reimport. Were any keys re-imported or recreated around that window?
Jordan: keys not re-imported — we checked KMS metadata and key-ids still present. CloudHSM user list unchanged. No rotation events from our scheduler at that time.
Ethan: mitigation steps: increase session_pool_size to 300 for crypto service (short-term), add exponential backoff + retry for CKR_DEVICE_ERROR, and route heavy ingest to a second cluster in us-east-1 (if available) while we confirm stability. For long-term: add healthcheck on HSM node that marks cluster unhealthy for new sessions during failover window so pool doesn't hand out sessions that will fail.
Priya: for compliance: we need the full CloudHSM audit logs (PKCS#11 call traces) for 09:08-09:18 UTC and confirm no plaintext or key material was written to our application logs. Also record the failover event in the incident log with RCA placeholders. Assign owners: Ethan -> infra/mitigation; Jordan -> support/customer comms & collect logs; Priya -> security/compliance review. ETA for initial customer update?
Jordan: I'll send a 1hr ack to customer and include that we're investigating root cause, collecting audit logs, and will recommend a mitigations plan. ETA 2h for next update.
Ethan: quick repro I ran locally against staging HSM: same pattern when I forcibly reboot one HSM node. Suggest applying circuit-breaker when >5% session checkout failures in 1m. Patch ready on branch hsm/pool-better-retry.
Priya: notes for audit: preserve logs in S3-retention-7y bucket, set immutable flag for the incident retention period. Also we need to confirm whether HSM failover is within acceptable SLA for customer (some regulated customers require no failover). Jordan — flag the account for dedicated capacity review.
Jordan: created incident INC-20260312-233 and uploaded initial logs (s3://redwood-incidents/INC-20260312-233/). Pushed customer ack.
Ethan: temporary runbook I'm going to execute now: 1) scale session pool 160->300, 2) deploy retry patch to canary, 3) enable cross-cluster fallback for decrypts (sticky by key -> try secondary cluster on CKR_DEVICE_ERROR). Will comment with PR links.
Priya: when you have the PKCS#11 audit bundle, share via secure link to security@redwood rather than slack. Do not paste PII or raw keys here.
Jordan: acknowledged. storing audit bundle in secure-share and notified security.
OpsBot: [ACTION] assigned INC-20260312-233 to Ethan, Jordan, Priya. Due 2026-03-12T12:00:00Z.
Jordan: thanks — will follow up after Ethan's canary. short-term: recommended customer backoff to 50-100 concurrency until we've validated.
Ethan: canary patch looks good — retries reduced transient 500s by ~95% on my test. Will roll to 10% traffic in 10m.
Priya: good. also add note to compliance ticket: confirm retention window for PKCS#11 logs is complete and that there are no gaps. If any gaps, escalate to AWS support for CloudHSM audit recovery.
Jordan: acknowledged. I'll update the customer with mitigation + ETA for permanent fix (pool changes + circuit-breaker) within 2h. :thumbsup:
Priya: thanks team. keep me looped if any unexpected key operations surface.
Ethan: will post PR and follow up in thread.
Jordan: closing loop here for now, moving to incident channel when we have RCA.
